title: TurboFNO: High-Performance Fourier Neural Operator with Fused FFT-GEMM-iFFT on GPU
problem: Fourier Neural Operators execute FFT, filtering, GEMM, and iFFT as separate stages, incurring multiple kernel launches and high memory traffic; lacks architecture-aware optimization.
motivation: FNO is widely used for PDE solvers but performance is sub-optimal; fusing kernels can reduce memory overhead and improve throughput.
method: Normally, Fourier Neural Operators split computation into four separate GPU operations (FFT, filtering, matrix multiplication, and inverse-FFT), with each launch moving data between fast and slow memory. TurboFNO fuses all four into a single continuous kernel that keeps data in fast GPU memory throughout. The implementation uses custom-written FFT and matrix multiplication code, strategically arranges data in memory (called "memory swizzling") to avoid slowdowns, and removes unnecessary zero-padding during computation.
key_novelty: This is the first implementation to fully fuse the three core operations (FFT, matrix multiplication, inverse-FFT) into a single GPU kernel, achieving 100% utilization of the GPU's shared memory and matching or exceeding NVIDIA's hand-optimized libraries cuBLAS and cuFFT.
contributions: Custom FFT kernel competitive with cuFFT with built-in optimizations
Custom GEMM kernel competitive with cuBLAS
Fused FFT-GEMM-iFFT kernel with 100% memory bank utilization
Up to 150% speedup vs. PyTorch, cuBLAS, cuFFT on A100
workloads: Fourier Neural Operators for PDE solving
limitations: A100-specific; large engineering effort; may not generalize to other GPU architectures; narrow workload (FNO only).
